memoryReview.evidence: Reviewed apps/rivals-fit-lab/README.md, hero-data.js, and app.config.json on this repository; did not obtain a rendered screenshot.
memoryReview.lesson: The predecessor provides quantitative hero vectors and paired-choice testing; the new application must distinguish tactical choice and mechanical comfort instead of copying the questionnaire.

memoryReview.evidence: Reviewed apps/rivals-roulette/app.config.json and documented wheel interaction; rendered screenshot was unavailable.
memoryReview.lesson: A spinning selection wheel favors random discovery; this product should create ranked, explainable results and direct interaction with a character dossier rather than a randomized pick.

references.observation: The official game organizes its roster into distinct characters and team interactions; role and ability differences underpin selection.
references.principle: Recommendations need character-specific mechanical profiles instead of pop-culture personality types.
references.application: Provide one indexed roster, distinct role labels, and ability-feature explanations for every character.
references.avoid: Do not copy official hero art into a local offline bundle without an appropriate license.

references.observation: The live game's hero lineup and roles change across releases, so a recommendation model needs a dated roster snapshot.
references.principle: A static offline knowledge model must disclose its update period and avoid presenting predicted win rates.
references.application: Label the date and character count, test dataset integrity and keep the model entirely playable offline.
references.avoid: Do not pretend manually scored character attributes are developer-certified gameplay statistics.

references.observation: The existing Pocket Works Fit Lab stores thirteen-dimensional hero vectors and paired-choice questions for fifty-three heroes.
references.principle: Reuse game-specific factual structure while designing a new player interaction and an updated roster.
references.application: Expand to fifty-four profiles, split ease from enjoyment and ask four battlefield decision scenarios.
references.avoid: Avoid reproducing the Fit Lab's paired-choice interface or implying identical scoring to that application.

concepts.medium: Native HTML semantic controls with app-authored CSS and embedded vector tactical schematics.
concepts.composition: A tall numbered page that treats a single question as the main tactical exhibit, followed by a ranked record of heroes.
concepts.interaction: Choose one of four action cards or drag a real preference slider, then inspect a character dossier with match feedback.
concepts.motion: Immediate ink-like selection and a subtle horizontal press shift, progressing to the next numbered case file.
concepts.rationale: Chosen because real quiz readability and immediate choices benefit from robust phone controls while vector battle scenarios provide a unique recognizable signature.

concepts.medium: Large painted raster character illustrations on swipeable fullscreen posters.
concepts.composition: One full-screen hero occupies the majority of the frame while questions hide behind each poster.
concepts.interaction: Swipe between illustrated heroes and reveal proposed personality matches by turning their posters.
concepts.motion: Long lateral poster flips and springlike overshoot during chapter navigation.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because posters consume the vertical phone area needed for detailed question choices and imply copyrighted character artwork.

concepts.medium: Custom canvas tactical arena with movable unit markers and a controllable map camera.
concepts.composition: The player looks down onto a full-screen battle map while situational questions appear as map labels.
concepts.interaction: Drag allied and enemy markers across a map to register the desired combat style and positioning.
concepts.motion: Dragged objects spring to nearby hexes with animated movement arcs and particle impacts.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because a map-heavy mini-game obscures the simple value judgment needed for twenty fast questions and raises accessibility complexity.

selection.reason: Text remains immediately readable, tactical diagrams stand out during battlefield scenarios, and user feedback updates results without loading a complex renderer.

rejected.reason: Too much reliance on large media and theatrical presentation at the expense of question density and offline responsiveness.
A freely draggable battle map would be a separate simulation and no longer accurately measure the player's preferred decisions.

tools.reason: The created installation icon is real authored SVG and the interactive battlefield diagrams are vector markup embedded in app-owned JavaScript.

assets.role: Standalone fingerprint and targeting-reticle icon for the Pocket Works app shelf and installed shortcut.
assets.acceptance: Legible contrasting fingerprint-reticle shape at very small launcher sizes, with no generic letter monogram.
assets.integration: Referenced in the local web manifest, favicon and Apple touch icon, with the export cached by the offline service worker.
assets.provenance: Original SVG drawing authored within this app, based on abstract reticle and DNA motifs with no third-party artwork.

risks: Long Russian answers can wrap on short portrait screens and bury the next question control.
On a phone the result lists must remain readable next to role insignia and numerical fit scores.
comparisons: Inspect initial versus first answered question at 390x844 and 1366x768 against the game quiz's intended hierarchy.
Inspect the complete 10-hero result next to character detail/modal and duo display on phone and desktop.
